indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer is a small U.S.-based oil and natural gas company, importing company, or freight company operating in states on the U.S. southwest border with transactional activity and profit margins that exceed the typical business profile of similar companies in their industries.
indicators.red_flag: Revenue / profit-margin above industry peer baseline (revenue-vs-operations anomaly)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D1 (Core transaction monitoring (deposit/account ledger)), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a business account whose transaction inflows are disproportionate to its declared revenue, headcount, payroll, or operating-expense footprint relative to industry peers, escalating when revenue appears decoupled from any observable operational activity.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days vs declared profile and peer cohort
build_logic.source: business deposit ledger joined to KYC business profile + industry peer benchmarks
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer is a small U.S.-based oil and natural gas company that is selling WTI crude oil and other types of crude oil for significantly less than the market rate.
indicators.red_flag: Crude sold below market rate (stolen-goods discount pricing)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D1 (Core transaction monitoring (deposit/account ledger)), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.window: rolling 90 days vs declared profile and peer cohort
build_logic.source: business deposit ledger joined to KYC business profile + industry peer benchmarks

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer is a small U.S.-based oil and natural gas company that is selling millions of dollars of crude oil per month but has no online presence or is using a basic website that appears designed to closely resemble major U.S. oil and natural gas companies’ websites in order to make their significant crude oil sales appear legitimate.
indicators.red_flag: High-revenue seller with absent / spoofed major-brand web presence (legitimacy-front)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer is a small U.S.-based oil and natural gas company that has a website indicating it is only a buyer or seller of crude oil, but the company is sending wire transfers to Mexican or U.S. companies for purchases of purported waste oil or other hazardous materials.
indicators.red_flag: Stated crude-only business vs waste-oil hazmat wire purchases (activity-vs-profile mismatch)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C22 (Trade-based money-laundering & documentary anomaly detection); data D5.

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer is a small U.S.-based oil and natural gas company that is suddenly purchasing waste oil or other hazardous materials from a singular or small number of Mexican and U.S. companies.
indicators.red_flag: Sudden waste-oil hazmat buying concentrated on few counterparties (single-source funnel)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C3 (Multi-originator funnel-in / fan-out network detection).

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer is a small U.S.-based oil and natural gas company that is sending wire transfers to Mexican or U.S. companies for waste oil or other hazardous materials without possessing the appropriate registrations with the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).
indicators.red_flag: Hazmat-purchase wires without required EPA registration (unlicensed-activity mismatch)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C22 (Trade-based money-laundering & documentary anomaly detection); data D15.

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer is a small U.S.-based oil and natural gas company that is sending wire transfers for waste oil or other hazardous materials to Mexican or U.S. companies that do not appear to be related to the oil and natural gas industry.
indicators.red_flag: Hazmat-purchase wires to out-of-industry payees (counterparty-sector mismatch)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C22 (Trade-based money-laundering & documentary anomaly detection); data D3.

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer is a small U.S.-based oil and natural gas company that has a sudden and significant volume of transactional activity with one or a small number of Mexican or U.S. companies that have little to no online presence and displays other indicators of illicit shell company activity.
indicators.red_flag: Concentrated volume with low-web-presence shell counterparties (shell-network funnel)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D10 (Customer & account reference / entity-resolution data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer is a small U.S.-based oil and natural gas company that is receiving domestic and international wire transfers for invoices related to the sale of crude oil but sending wire transfers to Mexican or U.S. companies for invoices for the purchase of waste oil or other hazardous materials.
indicators.red_flag: Crude-sale inflows recycled into hazmat-purchase outflows (invoice-relabel pass-through)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C22 (Trade-based money-laundering & documentary anomaly detection); data D3.

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer is a U.S. importing company that is receiving wire transfers from U.S.-based oil and natural gas companies and sending wire transfers to Mexican companies for invoices involving the U.S. importing company’s purchases of waste oil or other hazardous materials, despite the U.S. importing company lacking appropriate registrations from the EPA.
indicators.red_flag: Importer relay of oil-co inflows to Mexico as unregistered hazmat purchases (cross-border pass-through)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C2 (Rapid pass-through / flow-through (receive-and-forward) detection).

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer is a U.S. importing company that is receiving wire transfers from a small U.S.-based oil and natural gas company for the sale of waste oil or other hazardous materials and then wiring those funds to a singular or small number of companies in Mexico.
indicators.red_flag: Receive-and-forward to few Mexican payees (cross-border mule pass-through)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C2 (Rapid pass-through / flow-through (receive-and-forward) detection).

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer claims to be a U.S.-based company involved in the import of waste oil or other hazardous materials, but upon further review, appears to be a shell company of a Mexican company.
indicators.red_flag: U.S.-stated importer resolving to a Mexican-controlled shell (nominee-front)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag an entity exhibiting shell or front-company markers â opaque or circular beneficial ownership, shared registered addresses or directors, recent incorporation with no observable operations â escalating when nominees or addresses recur across a cluster of related entities.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days over the ownership/address graph
build_logic.source: corporate registry + KYC beneficial-ownership records + entity-resolution graph
build_logic.route: Tier-2 network alert â AML investigations gate

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer is a U.S. company that is the ultimate consignee of purchases of waste oil or other hazardous materials but is registered to a residential address.
indicators.red_flag: Hazmat consignee registered to a residential address (shell-address red flag)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D10 (Customer & account reference / entity-resolution data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators of Cartel Oil Smuggling Schemes
indicators.flag: A customer is a small U.S.-based oil and natural gas company, importing company, or freight company operating on the U.S. southwest border that is transacting with Mexican and U.S. companies and their beneficial owners associated with Cartel-related activity based on open-source reporting in Mexico, indictments, and OFAC designations and/or press releases.
indicators.red_flag: Counterparties / UBOs adverse-media- or OFAC-linked to cartels (sanctions / adverse-media nexus)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C18 (Sanctions / watchlist screening).
